40853-the-viking-blood-a-story-of-seafar.creator: Frederick William Wallace
40853-the-viking-blood-a-story-of-seafar.description: A book by Frederick William Wallace. some consideration, he added, "You may call him Percival also if you've set your mind on it, but remember, Donald comes first!" So Donald Percival McKenzie it was, and thus it is inscribed in the Register of Births for the City of Glasgow, in the County of Lanark, Scotland, in the year of our Lord, Eighteen Hundred and Seventy-six.

arxiv-2005-13017.title: Chaos on the hypercube
arxiv-2005-13017.creator: Yiyang Jia, and Jacobus J. M. Verbaarschot
arxiv-2005-13017.description: Abstract We analyze the spectral properties of a d d -dimensional HyperCubic (HC) lattice model originally introduced by Parisi. The U(1) gauge links of this model give rise to a magnetic flux of constant magnitude ϕ \phi but random orientation through the faces of the hypercube.

arxiv-2201-12496.title: A direct and elementary proof of the well-definedness of the interior and exterior polynomials of hypergraphs
arxiv-2201-12496.creator: Xiaxia Guan, Xian’an Jin, Tianlong Ma School of Mathematical Sciences, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian 361005, China E-mails: gxx0544@126.com; xajin@xmu.edu.cn; tianlongma@aliyun.com
arxiv-2201-12496.description: Abstract T. Kálmán (A version of Tutte’s polynomial for hypergraphs, Adv. Math. 244 (2013) 823-873.) introduced the interior and exterior polynomials which are generalizations of the Tutte polynomial T ⁡ ( x , y ) T(x,y) on plane points ( 1 / x , 1 ) (1/x,1) and ( 1 , 1 / y ) (1,1/y) to hypergraphs.

arxiv-2202-00618.title: Penalized Estimation of Frailty-Based Illness-Death Models for Semi-Competing Risks
arxiv-2202-00618.creator: Harrison T. Reeder, Junwei Lu, Sebastien J. Haneuse
arxiv-2202-00618.description: Abstract Semi-competing risks refers to the time-to-event analysis setting where the occurrence of a non-terminal event is subject to whether a terminal event has occurred, but not vice versa. Semi-competing risks arise in a broad range of clinical contexts, including studies of preeclampsia, a condition that may arise during pregnancy and for which delivery is a terminal event.

arxiv-2208-03312.title: How do the dynamics of the Milky Way - Large Magellanic Cloud system affect gamma-ray constraints on particle dark matter? 2022 How do the dynamics of the Milky Way - Large Magellanic Cloud system affect gamma-ray constraints on particle dark matter? – 11
arxiv-2208-03312.creator: Christopher Eckner, Francesca Calore, Denis Erkal, Sophia Lilleengen, Michael S. Petersen
arxiv-2208-03312.description: Abstract Previous studies on astrophysical dark matter (DM) constraints have all assumed that the Milky Way’s (MW) DM halo can be modelled in isolation. However, recent work suggests that the MW’s largest dwarf satellite, the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), has a mass of 10-20 % \% that of the MW and is currently merging with our Galaxy.

arxiv-2208-14819.title: Cadence Detection in Symbolic Classical Music using Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2208-14819.description: Abstract Cadences are complex structures that have been driving music from the beginning of contrapuntal polyphony until today. Detecting such structures is vital for numerous MIR tasks such as musicological analysis, key detection, or music segmentation. However, automatic cadence detection remains challenging mainly because it involves a combination of high-level musical elements like harmony, voice leading, and rhythm.

arxiv-2209-02347.title: Bulk-LDOS Correspondence in Topological Insulators
arxiv-2209-02347.creator: Biye Xie, Renwen Huang, Shiyin Jia, Zemeng Lin, Junzheng Hu, Yao Jiang, Shaojie Ma, Peng Zhan, Minghui Lu, Zhenlin Wang, Yanfeng Chen, Shuang Zhang

arxiv-2212-12423.title: Circular Figures in Elamite Mathematics
arxiv-2212-12423.creator: Nasser Heydari, Kazuo Muroi
arxiv-2212-12423.description: Abstract In this article, we study a particular group of plane figures whose constants are listed in the Susa Mathematical Tablet No. 3 ( SMT No. 3 ). We explain possible ways to define these figures and seek to demonstrate that the Susa scribes used complicated calculations to obtain such numbers.

arxiv-2302-08512.title: Generalized Survival Probability
arxiv-2302-08512.creator: David A. Zarate-Herrada 1 , Lea F. Santos 2 and E. Jonathan Torres-Herrera 1
arxiv-2302-08512.description: Abstract The survival probability measures the probability that a system taken out of equilibrium has not yet moved out from its initial state. Inspired by the generalized entropies used to analyze nonergodic states, we introduce a generalized version of the survival probability, and discuss how it can assist studies of the structure of the eigenstates and ergodicity.

arxiv-2306-12977.title: Sum-Rate Maximization of RSMA-based Aerial Communications with Energy Harvesting : A Reinforcement Learning Approach
arxiv-2306-12977.creator: Jaehyup Seong, Mesut Toka
arxiv-2306-12977.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jaehyup Seong, Mesut Toka. In this letter, we investigate a joint power and beamforming design problem for rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-based aerial communications with energy harvesting, where a self-sustainable aerial base station serves multiple users by utilizing the harvested energy.

arxiv-2402-10284.title: The intermediate neutron capture process Preprint: arthur.choplin@ulb.be Affiliation: Institut d’Astronomie et d’Astrophysique, Université Libre de Bruxelles, CP 226, B-1050 Brussels, Belgium
arxiv-2402-10284.creator: A. Choplin, L. Siess, S. Goriely, S. Martinet
arxiv-2402-10284.description: Abstract Context. The intermediate neutron capture process (i-process) can develop during proton ingestion events (PIE), potentially during the early stages of low-mass low-metallicity asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars. Aims. We examine the impact of overshoot mixing on the triggering and development of i-process nucleosynthesis in AGB stars of various initial masses and metallicities. Methods.

arxiv-2412-01326.title: Dynamical System Approach for Optimal Control Problems with Equilibrium Constraints Using Gap-Constraint-Based Reformulation
arxiv-2412-01326.creator: Kangyu Lin, Toshiyuki Ohtsuka
arxiv-2412-01326.description: Abstract Optimal control problems for nonsmooth dynamical systems governed by differential variational inequalities (DVI) are called optimal control problems with equilibrium constraints (OCPEC). It provides a general formalism for nonsmooth optimal control. However, solving OCPEC using the direct method (i.e., first-discretize-then-optimize) is challenging owing to the lack of correct sensitivity and constraint regularity.

arxiv-2505-12648.title: SafeMove-RL: A Certifiable Reinforcement Learning Framework for Dynamic Motion Constraints in Trajectory Planning
arxiv-2505-12648.creator: Tengfei Liu, Haoyang Zhong, Jiazheng Hu, Xiaoxu Liu, Tan Zhang
arxiv-2505-12648.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tengfei Liu, Haoyang Zhong, Jiazheng Hu, Xiaoxu Liu, Tan Zhang. This study presents a dynamic safety margin-based reinforcement learning framework for local motion planning in dynamic and uncertain environments. The proposed planner integrates real-time trajectory optimization with adaptive gap analysis, enabling effective feasibility assessment under partial observability constraints. To address safety-critical computations in unknown scenarios, an enhanced online learning mechanism is introduced, which dynamically corrects spatial trajectories by forming dynamic safety margins while maintaining control invariance.

arxiv-2509-22096.title: A Source of Deterministic Entanglement for Matter-Wave Networks
arxiv-2509-22096.creator: Chen Li, RuGway Wu, Jörg Schmiedmayer
arxiv-2509-22096.description: Abstract We describe a deterministic and experimentally feasible protocol for generating entangled pairs of ultracold neutral atoms through controlled dissociation of diatomic Feshbach molecules. The dissociation process naturally produces nonlocal quantum correlations in spin, position-momentum, and path degrees of freedom, enabling the deterministic preparation of Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs of massive particles and multiqubit states through hyperentangled encoding.

pmc-10734021.title: Versatile Ultrasound-Compatible Microfluidic Platform for In Vitro Microvasculature Flow Research and Imaging Optimization
pmc-10734021.creator: Tamar Mano, Tal Grutman, Tali Ilovitsh
pmc-10734021.description: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables the creation of super-resolved images and velocity maps by localizing and tracking microbubble contrast agents through a vascular network over thousands of frames of ultrafast plane wave images. However, a significant challenge lies in developing ultrasound-compatible microvasculature phantoms to investigate microbubble flow and distribution in controlled environments.

pmc-11609805.creator: Maksim Klimiankou, Ivan Tesakov, Grigorios Tsaknakis, Erasmia Boutakoglou, Irene Mavroudi, Malte Ritter, Marc Sturm, Julia Skokowa, Helen A. Papadaki
pmc-11609805.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). fections, is constantly growing.1 While most patients with CN receive a genetic diagnosis based on the known causative genes, 22% of CN patients, according to the Severe Congenital Neutropenia International Registry database, do not have an identified genetic mutation.2 In this study, we performed whole exome sequencing (WES) and prioritization of variants in three non-consanguineous families with genetically unclassified neutropenia after negative Sanger sequencing of ELANE, HAX1, and JAGN1, genes most frequently associated with CN.

pmc-11816515.title: Contacts with health services for COVID-19-related reasons during the first wave of the pandemic in Portugal: a longitudinal study
pmc-11816515.creator: Mónica Granja, Daniela Correia, Luís Alves, Milton Severo, Raquel Lucas, Sofia Correia, Ana Cristina Santos
pmc-11816515.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction Access to COVID-19-related care during the pandemic deserve attention and study to inform future strategies to deal with similar health emergencies in the future. We aimed to describe access to care for COVID-19-related reasons during the first 9 weeks of the pandemic in Portugal, to quantify the frequency of remote and in-person contacts with healthcare for COVID-19-related reasons and to assess the association between individual and context characteristics and contacts with health services.

pmc-12694318.title: Ultrafast Laser-Enabled 3D Glass Microchannel Reactors
pmc-12694318.creator: Xiaolong Li, Jinxin Huang, Jian Xu, Ya Cheng
pmc-12694318.description: Microchannel reactors are among the most important tools used for high-performance continuous-flow synthesis. However, most microchannel reactors manufactured with conventional micromachining techniques are limited to two-dimensional (2D) planar geometries, which pose significant challenges for the custom production of three-dimensional (3D) architectures that offer superior microchemical performance.

pmc-12901458.title: Zika virus infection disturbs development of human muscle progenitor cells
pmc-12901458.creator: Cássia Rocha, Daniella Arêas Mendes-da-Cruz, Elisa Negroni, Vincent Mouly, Ieda Pereira Ribeiro, Myrna Cristina Bonaldo, Wilson Savino, Vinicius Cotta-de-Almeida, Dumith Chequer Bou-Habib, Ingo Riederer
pmc-12901458.description: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection has emerged as a global public health emergency due to its expansion capacity and ability to cause neurological and congenital diseases. Muscle cells are targets for ZIKV, and myalgia and muscle disorders are frequently related symptoms during infection.

pmc-13156640.title: Biological age acceleration, genetic susceptibility, and incident diabetic retinopathy risk: A prospective cohort study
pmc-13156640.creator: Yuxuan Wang, Lifeng Wang
pmc-13156640.description: BackgroundDiabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a major microvascular complication of diabetes, and conventional risk factors do not fully explain individual differences in disease risk. This study investigated the associations of biological age acceleration with incident DR.MethodsThis prospective cohort study included 12,608 UK Biobank participants with diabetes.

pmc-13194664.title: Development and Validation of the Self-Efficacy Scale for Bharatanatyam Dancers
pmc-13194664.creator: Swarnamalya M, D C Mathangi, Padmavathi, Mahesh Kumar
pmc-13194664.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSelf-efficacy, the belief in one’s ability to succeed, plays a crucial role in learning, consistent practice and performance in skill-intensive fields. Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance form, requires high levels of technical precision, artistic expression and physical endurance. While research in sports and Western dance has shown that self-efficacy enhances performance, there is limited evidence in Indian classical dance, and no validated self-efficacy tool specific to Bharatanatyam exists. Standard scales do not capture the cultural, physical and expressive dimensions of Bharatanatyam.

pmc-13316822.title: Patterns of Scabies Treatment Among Syrian Dermatologists: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13316822.creator: Rahaf Toutounji, Luma Haj Kassem, Mohamad Nabhan Sawas, Mohammed Abdulrazzak, Silva Ishkanian
pmc-13316822.description: IntroductionScabies, caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, remains a significant public health problem in Syria, where socioeconomic hardship and overcrowding contribute to persistent transmission. This study examines current treatment practices among Syrian dermatologists and evaluates the extent to which these practices align with internationally recommended management approaches.MethodsA structured online questionnaire was administered to 159 dermatologists across multiple Syrian provinces.

pmc-13330286.title: CD163+ macrophages coordinate erythroblastic Island formation and iron metabolism to enable glucocorticoid-induced erythropoiesis
pmc-13330286.creator: Mengjia Li, Yaomei Wang, Hong Huang, Hao Sun, Mengya Gao, Mingxia Sun, Xudong Li, Zexing Liu, Donghao Liu, Meimei Yan, Zhenghua Huang, Zhen Zhang, Yuhan Hu, Bozheng Wang, Yiwei Zhou, Siyue Li, Yu An, Miao Liu, Yupeng Liu, Fengcai Gao, Fangfang Ge, Wenjuan Fan, Hao Wang, Xing Li, Fang Wang, Guomei Fu, Shiyu Zuo, Binglei Zhang, Jinxin Miao, Chong Wang, Yongping Song, Xiuli An, Weijie Cao, Linping Xu, Wei Li, Zhilei Bian

pmc-13391957.title: Global burden and temporal trends of kidney cancer among children from 1990 to 2021: an analysis with projections to 2036
pmc-13391957.creator: Kai Liu, Changlin Yang, Feng Chen, Xuhua Qiao, Yujie Geng, Chundong Ji
pmc-13391957.description: BackgroundChildhood kidney cancer (KC), the third most prevalent pediatric solid malignancy, remains incompletely characterized in terms of epidemiological patterns and health inequities. This study aimed to analyze global trends, inequalities, and future burden of childhood KC from 1990 to 2021.

pmc-13450599.title: Morning peak and high prevalence of pulmonary embolism and psychiatric disorders in women with sudden cardiac arrest: results from the ReCaPTa study
pmc-13450599.creator: Youcef Azeli, Eneko Barbería, Alberto Fernández, Inés Landín, Cristina Rey-Reñones, Silvia García-Vilana, Nina Vidal-González, Gil Bonet, Xavier Jiménez-Fàbrega, Alfredo Bardají
pmc-13450599.description: BackgroundSudden cardiac arrest (SCA) in women remains understudied, often leading to generalised approaches. We aimed to identify sex-specific differences in the clinical profile, risk factors, and causes of SCA to guide targeted interventions.MethodsThis prospective population-based study (ReCaPTa) analysed out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in a region of Spain (2014–2017). Data were triangulated from Emergency Medical Services, hospital records, and forensic autopsies.
